newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade puts Polish wheat import at 0.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: German trade puts Polish wheat import at 0.5 mln T.

text.p: Poland has bought up to 500,000 tonnes of West European wheat since September, nearly all from Germany, traders estimated on Thursday.
At least six international traders and large cooperatives were involved.

But sources were reluctant to forecast future business because they could not gauge Poland's readiness to accept the quantity already agreed -- given that prices were now easing -- and because of logistics problems.
"Poland has been buying actively since September but their buyers are now trying to get out of some expensive contracts," a trader with a large international grain house said.
"Delivery by train is ongoing but ports are now blocked because of limited handling capacity and slow discharge."
Polish demand has kept German wheat prices at the highest levels in Europe while volume pressure has been weighing down prices elsewhere.
Polish trades were reported at 290-295 marks a tonne fob for 12.5 percent protein bread wheat.
"Sellers say they need that money to make it worthwile," said one broker.
"Rail trucks have been returned slowly or not at all...it's holding up the exports and adding to costs."
Traders also said some of the contracts might filled with North American grain if prices there proved to be more attractive or if Brussels failed to grant enough licences.
